claims.statement: The Egyptian Ministry’s overview dates the Predynastic period to about 5500–3100 BCE.

value.text: The Egyptian Ministry’s overview dates the Predynastic period to about 5500–3100 BCE.

claims.statement: Nile Valley communities developed distinct regional cultures before Egyptian political unification.

value.text: Nile Valley communities developed distinct regional cultures before Egyptian political unification.

claims.statement: The ministry places Badarian culture around 5500–4000 BCE near modern Asyut.

value.text: The ministry places Badarian culture around 5500–4000 BCE near modern Asyut.

claims.statement: The Maadi cultural complex developed near modern Cairo around 4000–3100 BCE.

value.text: The Maadi cultural complex developed near modern Cairo around 4000–3100 BCE.

claims.statement: Naqada I is dated around 4000–3500 BCE in Upper Egypt.

value.text: Naqada I is dated around 4000–3500 BCE in Upper Egypt.

claims.statement: The ministry describes increasing social differentiation towards the period’s end.

value.text: The ministry describes increasing social differentiation towards the period’s end.

claims.statement: The Met dates the Old Kingdom to approximately 2649–2130 BCE.

value.text: The Met dates the Old Kingdom to approximately 2649–2130 BCE.

claims.statement: Much of the surviving evidence for material culture comes from funerary contexts.

value.text: Much of the surviving evidence for material culture comes from funerary contexts.

claims.statement: Djoser’s reign is dated approximately 2649–2630 BCE in this chronology.

value.text: Djoser’s reign is dated approximately 2649–2630 BCE in this chronology.

claims.statement: His Saqqara funerary complex included Egypt’s first pyramid.

value.text: His Saqqara funerary complex included Egypt’s first pyramid.

claims.statement: The Met places Khufu’s reign around 2551–2528 BCE.

value.text: The Met places Khufu’s reign around 2551–2528 BCE.

claims.statement: The Great Pyramid at Giza belongs to Khufu.

value.text: The Great Pyramid at Giza belongs to Khufu.

claims.statement: The New Kingdom is dated approximately 1550–1070 BCE.

value.text: The New Kingdom is dated approximately 1550–1070 BCE.

claims.statement: Theban royal tombs and mortuary temples supported elaborate funerary traditions.

value.text: Theban royal tombs and mortuary temples supported elaborate funerary traditions.

claims.statement: A settlement in western Thebes housed artists who made royal tombs.

value.text: A settlement in western Thebes housed artists who made royal tombs.

claims.statement: Around 3200 BCE, Uruk was a major city in southern Mesopotamia.

value.text: Around 3200 BCE, Uruk was a major city in southern Mesopotamia.

claims.statement: Clay pictographs recorded goods and workers’ rations, preceding later cuneiform.

value.text: Clay pictographs recorded goods and workers’ rations, preceding later cuneiform.

claims.statement: The Met dates the Early Dynastic period to 2900–2350 BCE.

value.text: The Met dates the Early Dynastic period to 2900–2350 BCE.

claims.statement: City rulers acquired luxury materials through trade and conquest.

value.text: City rulers acquired luxury materials through trade and conquest.

claims.statement: The Met dates the flourishing urban Indus civilization to approximately 2600–1900 BCE.

value.text: The Met dates the flourishing urban Indus civilization to approximately 2600–1900 BCE.

claims.statement: Harappa and Mohenjo Daro were large settlements connected with western trading partners.

value.text: Harappa and Mohenjo Daro were large settlements connected with western trading partners.

claims.statement: Seals preserve writing that remains undeciphered.

value.text: Seals preserve writing that remains undeciphered.

claims.statement: The Shang dynasty is dated approximately 1600–1046 BCE.

value.text: The Shang dynasty is dated approximately 1600–1046 BCE.

claims.statement: Its political centre lay along the Yellow River in present-day Henan.

value.text: Its political centre lay along the Yellow River in present-day Henan.

claims.statement: The Western Zhou period is dated 1046–771 BCE.

value.text: The Western Zhou period is dated 1046–771 BCE.

claims.statement: Zhou rulers exercised authority across much of central China.

value.text: Zhou rulers exercised authority across much of central China.

claims.statement: The Eastern Zhou period is dated 770–256 BCE.

value.text: The Eastern Zhou period is dated 770–256 BCE.

claims.statement: After the capital moved to Luoyang, regional states became increasingly autonomous.

value.text: After the capital moved to Luoyang, regional states became increasingly autonomous.

claims.statement: The Western Han period lasted from 206 BCE to 9 CE.

value.text: The Western Han period lasted from 206 BCE to 9 CE.

claims.statement: Chang’an was its capital, with palaces, residential wards and market areas.

value.text: Chang’an was its capital, with palaces, residential wards and market areas.

claims.statement: The Eastern Han period lasted from 25 to 220 CE.

value.text: The Eastern Han period lasted from 25 to 220 CE.

claims.statement: Its capital was Luoyang; diplomacy and long-distance exchange expanded.

value.text: Its capital was Luoyang; diplomacy and long-distance exchange expanded.

claims.statement: Emperor Wu ruled during 141–87 BCE.

value.text: Emperor Wu ruled during 141–87 BCE.

claims.statement: His reign promoted Confucian learning in official conduct and education.

value.text: His reign promoted Confucian learning in official conduct and education.

claims.statement: Olmec cultural and artistic activity flourished around 1200–400 BCE in Veracruz and Tabasco.

value.text: Olmec cultural and artistic activity flourished around 1200–400 BCE in Veracruz and Tabasco.

claims.statement: Sculptors used imported volcanic stone and jade.

value.text: Sculptors used imported volcanic stone and jade.

claims.statement: After about 900 BCE, La Venta developed platforms and a major pyramid.

value.text: After about 900 BCE, La Venta developed platforms and a major pyramid.

claims.statement: Monumental building and carving there ceased after about 400 BCE.

value.text: Monumental building and carving there ceased after about 400 BCE.

claims.statement: UNESCO reports Caral’s development between approximately 3000 and 1800 BCE.

value.text: UNESCO reports Caral’s development between approximately 3000 and 1800 BCE.

claims.statement: Its architecture includes large platform mounds and sunken circular courts.

value.text: Its architecture includes large platform mounds and sunken circular courts.

claims.statement: UNESCO’s reference position places Caral in Peru’s Supe Valley.
UNESCO describes Kush as a major power from the eighth century BCE to the fourth century CE.

value.text: UNESCO describes Kush as a major power from the eighth century BCE to the fourth century CE.

value.text: The Meroe region preserves royal, religious, domestic and water-management remains.
